cases.query: Summarize history within model input limits with safe fallback. Orchestrate budget-aware history summarization by deriving a non-negative history budget from model input capacity, propagating that budget to the summarizer, selecting the maximal fitting older-message prefix while retaining the recent conversational tail, and preserving the complete original context with an observable warning if summary generation fails.

Derive a history budget from model input capacity. Compute an explicit, non-negative history budget from the summarizer or main model's input-token capability, applying an appropriate safety margin and exposing the resolved budget to downstream summarization logic.

Preserve original context when summarization fails. Recover from summary-generation failure by returning the original messages unchanged and emitting an observable warning, avoiding both context loss and session failure.

Select the maximal history prefix that fits a summarizer budget. Choose as many older messages as fit within the available summarizer input budget while preserving the recent message tail needed for conversational continuity; selection should remain within budget and grow monotonically as capacity increases.

Bind a capacity policy to the effective routed reservation. Resolve the mandatory downstream reservation for the current routed target using the same precedence as request execution, then pass it explicitly with route-specific capacity metadata to the policy calculator. Prefer the durable request-envelope cap, fall back to the adapter or model default, and use the host-defined missing-cap value only when neither exists. Re-resolve on route changes and keep this reservation distinct from auxiliary-operation output caps.

Repair and validate proactive pressure against residual shared capacity. Diagnose a proactive compaction gate that is derived from nominal capacity even though the routed request reserves output from the same finite capacity; bind the current route’s effective output reservation and capacity metadata; derive pressure and retention budgets from the remaining capacity; normalize pressure headroom and auxiliary-summary cap defaults without conflating them with the routed reservation; reject invalid route-specific budgets; and validate arithmetic, route switching, configuration composition, deterministic compaction continuation, and applicable live-provider behavior.

Default an auxiliary output cap from configured pressure headroom. When one policy owns both proactive pressure headroom and an auxiliary generation limit, use the resolved headroom as the auxiliary output-cap default only when no explicit cap is configured. Preserve global and target-specific explicit caps according to specificity, require the final auxiliary cap to be positive, and do not conflate it with the separate reservation of the routed primary request.

Derive a proactive threshold from residual shared capacity. When upstream workload, a mandatory downstream reservation, and safety headroom share one finite capacity, derive the proactive pressure threshold from the residual budget rather than nominal capacity alone. Compute available message capacity after reservation, subtract pressure headroom, cap the nominal ratio threshold by that residual amount, resolve retention according to its declared basis, and reject configurations whose budgets or retention relation are invalid.

Derive a policy threshold from residual shared capacity. When upstream work and a downstream reservation consume the same bounded resource, subtract the normalized reservation from nominal capacity and apply the threshold policy and its safety guards to that residual capacity.

Repair a derived threshold when downstream work reserves shared capacity. Diagnose a threshold computed from nominal capacity despite a downstream reservation against the same resource, normalize the reservation, derive the threshold and safety guards from residual capacity, propagate reservation state through construction and reconfiguration, and validate numeric and boundary behavior.

Normalize an optional capacity reservation before arithmetic. Convert an optional or malformed reservation input into either a positive integer reservation or an explicit no-reservation state before using it in capacity calculations.

Recompute derived capacity policy state during reconfiguration. Carry a capacity reservation as runtime policy state, define whether an omitted reconfiguration value preserves it and whether an explicit value replaces it, then recompute all derived thresholds after the active capacity or reservation changes.

Validate boundary partitions for shared-capacity policies. Partition reservation states around the shared-capacity boundary and verify an explicit behavior for absent, invalid, non-positive, ordinary positive, near-capacity, and capacity-exceeding reservations.

Account for every context-visible artifact. Measure context pressure from the complete representation sent or made visible to the model, including custom session entries rather than only ordinary messages. Use the same canonical conversion for token accounting and compaction cut-point selection.

Maintain model-aware compaction through the next request boundary. Orchestrate compaction by resolving validated provider/model-specific reserve and retention settings, propagating the active policy across reconfiguration and every compaction path, measuring pressure from all context-visible session artifacts, and evaluating that pressure immediately before the next real provider request. If a tool result terminates the turn, skip request preparation and avoid unnecessary compaction.

Place pressure checks at the next real request boundary. Evaluate automatic compaction pressure immediately before a real next provider request rather than unconditionally after a tool result. This prevents unnecessary compaction when a tool outcome terminates the turn while ensuring an over-budget context is compacted before a continuing request begins.

Replay resolved policy across runtime reconfiguration. Re-resolve or propagate the active model-dependent policy whenever runtime state or execution path changes, preventing manual compaction, automatic checks, overflow recovery, extension preparation, and model switching from using stale or divergent settings.

Resolve model-specific policy with validated fallback. Resolve compaction parameters such as reserveTokens and keepRecentTokens using exact provider/model precedence over base settings, while validating both base and override values as safe integers. Return one active policy plus its resolution provenance so callers can apply predictable fallback behavior.

Recompute derived capacity policy state during reconfiguration. Carry a capacity reservation as runtime policy state, define whether an omitted reconfiguration value preserves it and whether an explicit value replaces it, then recompute all derived thresholds after the active capacity or reservation changes.

Derive proactive policies from residual shared capacity. When upstream processing and mandatory downstream work consume the same bounded capacity, normalize and bind the effective downstream reservation, subtract it from nominal capacity, and derive proactive thresholds, retention limits, and safety guards from the residual capacity. Propagate reservation state through construction and reconfiguration, recompute dependent policies when the route or capacity changes, and reject or explicitly handle exhausted or non-positive residual budgets rather than masking them with final-result clamping.

diagnostics.interpretation: Graph mode is an expansion/context experiment; its self-retrieval rank is not an end-task success metric.

limitations: The catalog contains only four evidence-grounded cases and one Pattern.
Expected targets are node-level self-retrieval, not end-task success.
Token counts are serialized title/summary characters divided by four, not model tokenizer counts.
No LLM is called during retrieval; semantic judging remains an admission/offline operation.
